precepts.text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints. These are the angels that bring your prayers before the Most High God.
precepts.point: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. His prayers and his alms came up for a memorial before God, and the angel told him to send men to Joppa and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The angel tells Cornelius, “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” How do prayers come up before God? Tobit shows it. The angel Raphael says, “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.”

These are the angels that bring your prayers before the Most High God. Cornelius saw “an angel of God coming in to him” about the ninth hour, and that angel came because his prayers had gone up and been presented before the Holy One.

So when Acts 10 says his prayers and alms came up “for a memorial before God”, it is speaking of this very thing: the holy angels going in and out before the glory of God, presenting the prayers of those who fear him.

And the answer came back down by the same way. The angel told Cornelius to send men to Joppa and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter, who would tell him what he ought to do.

precepts.text: Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. When you pray to God, if you combine it with alms and fasting, the prayers are heard before the Most High. That is exactly what we read of Cornelius in Acts 10:2 and 10:4.
precepts.point: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. His prayers and his alms came up for a memorial before God, and the angel told him to send men to Joppa and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
In the same chapter where Raphael says he presents the prayers of the saints, he says what makes those prayers go up: “Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.” Prayer joined with fasting and alms and being righteous is what makes your prayers go before the Lord.

In other words, when you pray to God and combine it with alms and fasting, the prayers are heard before the Most High. That is exactly what we read of Cornelius in Acts 10:2: “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.”

And it is exactly what the angel told him in Acts 10:4: “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” Not his prayers alone, but his prayers and his alms together, from a devout man who kept the law.

So Cornelius is the example of what Tobit teaches. His righteousness, his alms and his praying alway went up before God, and God answered by sending him to Peter.

precepts.text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints: because they minister unto us; they are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers. They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose people. That is popular persuasion; that is lies.
precepts.point: John fell at the angel's feet to worship him, and he said, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren. The angels are our brethren; the angels have tribes too. In Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels at the twelve gates stand each at the gate of their tribe.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Now Raphael makes himself known: “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” The one Tobit called brother, Azarias of his brethren, was the angel all along.

Why do the angels present the prayers of the saints? Because they minister unto us. They are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers.

They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose the people that inhabit this place called the United Snakes of America. That is untrue. That is popular persuasion; that is lies. The world is being taught to call what comes out of the heavens demons and fallen angels, so that it will gather to fight against Christ and his army. But the angels are our brethren, fellowservants who keep the testimony of Jesus, and we worship God alone.

precepts.why: Tobit is in the Apocrypha, the book the white man says is not canon, you're not supposed to read that. Ah, shut the hell up; you don't tell us what to read. They took that out first from the slaves: some of these slaves know how to read, get rid of that, especially in the Caribbean islands, because they were using the book of Maccabees as fuel for insurrection to fight against the slave masters. “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” So now we know the name of the one of these seven angels who deals with the prayers of Israel, that deals with the incense. Now you can put a name to this angel in Revelation 8:3: this is Raphael. All the prayers we make to the Father go up, and Raphael makes sure they go before the Lord.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “But write all things which are done in a book”: see what the angel told Tobit. The Apocrypha was always part of the Bible; it was in the Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate.
